summary: Creating OAuth credentials in Google Cloud is quick, but shipping a public app that touches Gmail, Drive, or Calendar user data is the hardest approval path in this set. Sensitive scopes trigger Google's OAuth app verification; restricted scopes (such as Gmail message bodies) additionally require an independent CASA security assessment and annual re-verification. Plan for weeks, not days, before a public app leaves the unverified state.

oauthAvailability.note: OAuth 2.0 is the standard for accessing Google APIs. Verification requirements scale with the sensitivity of the scopes you request.
alternatives: Service accounts for server-to-server access without a user present

difficulty.reason: Restricted scopes require OAuth verification plus an independent CASA security assessment and annual re-verification.

handsOn.note: Includes consent-screen config, scope justification, and assessment prep.

approvalWait.note: Dominated by verification and, for restricted scopes, the CASA assessment.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: The OAuth app verification plus CASA security assessment for restricted scopes dominates the timeline.

review.requiredWhen: Required when a public app requests sensitive or restricted scopes. Apps using only non-sensitive scopes may skip verification (brand verification still applies to show a name and logo).

stages.name: OAuth app verification
stages.description: Google reviews the app, consent screen, scope justifications, and a demo video for sensitive/restricted scopes.

stages.name: CASA security assessment
stages.description: Independent CASA assessment required for restricted scopes (e.g. Gmail message content). Must be repeated for annual re-verification.

prerequisites.detail: OAuth client credentials are created inside a Cloud project.
App name, support email, developer contact, authorized domains, and a privacy policy are required.

prerequisites.item: A verified domain and public privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Authorized domains must be verified; a homepage and privacy policy URL are required for verification.

prerequisites.item: Scope justifications and a demo video
prerequisites.detail: Sensitive/restricted scope requests need written justification and a walkthrough video.

steps.title: Create OAuth client credentials in Google Cloud
steps.detail: In the Google API Console, create an OAuth client ID appropriate for your platform (Web application for server-side or JavaScript web apps). A JavaScript app needs no secret; a web-server app does.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Set the app name, user support email, developer contact, authorized domains, and links to your homepage and privacy policy. Add the scopes your app needs; the console labels each as non-sensitive, sensitive, or restricted.
steps.gotcha: Adding even one sensitive or restricted scope moves a public app into the verification requirement.

steps.title: Select the minimum scopes and justify them
steps.detail: Pick the narrowest Gmail/Drive/Calendar scopes that satisfy your feature. For each sensitive or restricted scope, write a justification explaining why the app needs it and record a demo video.

steps.title: Submit for OAuth app verification
steps.detail: Submit the app for verification from the consent-screen page. Google reviews scopes, branding, and your justification. Expect follow-up questions.

steps.title: Complete the CASA assessment for restricted scopes
steps.detail: If any scope is restricted (for example reading Gmail message content), complete an independent CASA security assessment through the App Defense Alliance. Restricted-scope apps must re-verify annually.

notes: Authorized redirect URIs are configured on the OAuth client in the Cloud console and must match exactly.
Authorized JavaScript origins are separate from redirect URIs for browser-side clients.

recommended.purpose: Basic sign-in; non-sensitive, no verification required.

sensitive.consequence: Restricted scope: triggers OAuth verification and a CASA security assessment, plus annual re-verification.
Full Drive access is restricted; prefer drive.file for per-file access to avoid the heaviest review.
Sensitive scope: requires OAuth app verification for public apps.

notes: Scope categories (non-sensitive, sensitive, restricted) are shown automatically when you add them in the console.
Using only non-sensitive scopes avoids mandatory verification; brand verification still lets you show a name and logo.

blockers.title: Unverified app warning blocks users
blockers.symptom: Users see an "unverified app" screen or cannot grant consent.
blockers.cause: A public app requesting sensitive/restricted scopes has not completed verification.
blockers.resolution: Complete OAuth app verification (and CASA for restricted scopes), or restrict the app to test users while in development.

blockers.title: CASA assessment rejected or stalled
blockers.symptom: Restricted-scope verification stalls pending the security assessment.
blockers.cause: The independent CASA assessment found gaps or is still in progress.
blockers.resolution: Address the assessor's findings and resubmit; budget several weeks and plan for annual re-verification.

blockers.title: Over-broad scope request rejected
blockers.symptom: Google asks you to remove or narrow scopes.
blockers.cause: The app requested broader scopes than its features justify (e.g. full Drive instead of drive.file).
blockers.resolution: Switch to the narrowest scope that works and resubmit with updated justification.

agentCan: Create the OAuth client and wire the token exchange and refresh
Draft scope justifications and the list of narrowest scopes
humanMust: Own the OAuth consent screen, branding, and privacy policy
Submit for verification and respond to Google's questions
Engage and pass the CASA security assessment for restricted scopes
handoffPoints: The agent prepares credentials and scope justifications; a human submits verification and drives the CASA assessment.

difficulty.note: Verification + CASA requirement confirmed on the verification help page.

timeEstimate.note: Wait times are community-reported; Google does not publish fixed durations.

prerequisites.note: Consent-screen and credential prerequisites from official docs.

steps.note: Steps follow the OAuth2 overview and verification help.

redirectUris.note: Redirect URI handling from the OAuth2 overview.

scopes.note: Scope list and categories from the Gmail scopes reference and verification help.
